name: New Kingdom of Egypt
alt: Eighteenth, Nineteenth and Twentieth Dynasties of Egypt

predecessors.name: Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt
predecessors.text: Thebes and Upper Egypt up to Cusae, the land of Kamose and Ahmose I

predecessors.name: Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt (Hyksos)
predecessors.text: Avaris, Memphis and the Delta taken from the Hyksos

predecessors.name: Hyksos
predecessors.text: Sharuhen 'near Gaza', the Hyksos stronghold taken after a three-year siege

successors.name: Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt
successors.text: Smendes at Tanis, who 'controlled Lower Egypt' (21st Dynasty page); the High Priests of Amun at Thebes 'effectively ruled Middle and Upper Egypt in all but name'

successors.name: Kingdom of Kush
successors.text: 'With the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC, Kush became an independent kingdom centered at Napata'

ledger.x: c. 1550: Ahmose I of Thebes founds the Eighteenth Dynasty and the New Kingdom. 'Ahmose... was the founder of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt'; Thebes 'became the capital for the whole of Egypt'. Dates differ by page: reign 1570-1546, 1560-1537, 1551-1527 or 1539-1514 BC (Ahmose I), 'Rise: c. 1570 BC'…

c. 1550: Ahmose I takes Avaris and ends Hyksos rule in Egypt. 'These records indicate that Ahmose I led three attacks against Avaris'... 'in the fourth attack, he conquered the city'; 'Ahmose would have conquered Avaris by the 18th or 19th year of his reign at the very latest'. The Seventeenth Dynasty page has a…

c. 1547: Ahmose I takes Sharuhen. 'conquering their stronghold Sharuhen near Gaza after a three-year siege'. The page gives no year for the siege; -1547 bridges three years from the fall of Avaris. [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Sharuhen page (tried for the thin item): 'The armies of Pharaoh Ahmose I…

c. 1540: Ahmose I restores Egyptian rule over Lower Nubia from Buhen. 'Ahmose restored Egyptian rule over Nubia, which was controlled from a new administrative center established at Buhen'; Aata and Tetian rebel and are crushed. No year on the page; -1540 sits inside the reign. Kamose had campaigned…

c. 1504: Thutmose I annexes Nubia. 'Thutmose I occupied Kush and destroyed its capital, Kerma'; 'annexation of Nubia c. 1504 BC'; 'Around 1500 BC, Nubia was absorbed into the New Kingdom of Egypt'. The Fourth Cataract is the southern limit (Thutmose III, year 50: 'only went so far as the fourth cataract of the Nile').
May 1457: Thutmose III takes Megiddo and the Canaanite princes pay tribute.
1447: Thutmose III reaches the Euphrates.
1445: Mitanni meets Thutmose at Aleppo.
1438: Thutmose III's last recorded Syrian campaign.
c. 1352: Akhenaten moves the capital to Amarna (Akhetaten). Infobox: 'Amarna c. 1352-1336 BC Akhenaten of Dynasty XVIII'.

c. 1352: the Syrian cities are lost. 'Egypt had not held Kadesh since the time of Akhenaten' and 'the Hittites had gradually extended their influence into the Levant'. The page gives no year; -1352 is Akhenaten's accession as the infobox dates the Amarna capital (bridging). [Reviewer me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Region was…
c. 1336: the court returns to Thebes. Infobox: 'Thebes c. 1336-1279 BC Dynasty XVIII and Dynasty XIX (until Ramesses II)'.
1295: the Nineteenth Dynasty begins.
c. 1279: Ramesses II moves the capital to Pi-Ramesses. Infobox: 'Pi-Ramesses c. 1279-1213 BC Ramesses II of Dynasty XIX'.

c. 1275: Ramesses II retakes Amurru. In his fourth year he 'marched north into Syria to recapture Amurru' (c. 1275 BC); the page notes Seti I's earlier capture of Kadesh and Amurru and that 'both regions may have lapsed back under Hittite control'.
1275: Egyptians and Hittites fight for the Orontes.
May 1274: Kadesh is fought and Egypt withdraws to Canaan.
1258: Ramesses II and Hattusili III make peace.
c. 1213: the capital returns to Memphis. Infobox: 'Memphis c. 1213-1069 BC Dynasty XIX (from Merneptah) and Dynasty XX'.
By 1200: Egypt gives up the Dongola Reach.
1189: the Twentieth Dynasty begins.

c. 1136: Egyptian Canaan ends. Ramesses VI page: 'Egypt lost control of its last strongholds in Canaan around the time of Ramesses VI's reign'; 'Egyptian presence in Canaan was terminated during or soon after Ramesses VI's rule, with the last garrisons leaving southern and western Palestine'; infobox reign…

c. 1136: the Gaza coast, the last Egyptian holding on the Cliopatria -1150 shape, goes with the rest of Egyptian Palestine. Ramesses VI page: 'the last garrisons leaving southern and western Palestine around the time' (reign c.1144-1136 BC). The page names no city; Gaza and Sharuhen are my reading of…

c. 1077: Kush goes its own way. 'With the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC, Kush became an independent kingdom centered at Napata.' Rounded to 1077, the death of Ramesses XI. [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18]…
1077: the New Kingdom ends with Ramesses XI; Egypt divides between Tanis and Thebes.

wars.name: Ahmose I's reconquest of Egypt from the Hyksos
wars.outcome: Theban victory: Avaris falls (the fourth attack) and the Hyksos are followed to Sharuhen, which falls after a three-year siege.

wars.name: Thutmose I's conquest of Kerma and Nubia
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: Kerma destroyed, Nubia annexed c.

wars.name: Thutmose III's Syrian campaigns
wars.outcome: Egyptian victories: Megiddo (9 May 1457 BC), Simyra (1450), the Euphrates crossing (1447), the Mitanni army met at Aleppo (1445); Canaan and Syria pay tribute, Kadesh not taken in year 42.

wars.name: Egyptian-Hittite War of Ramesses II (Battle of Kadesh)
wars.outcome: Drawn battle at Kadesh (May 1274 BC); the Hittites keep Kadesh and Amurru, Egypt keeps Canaan; Ramesses II and Hattusili III make peace in 1258 BC.

wars.name: Sea Peoples and Libyan invasions under Ramesses III
wars.outcome: Egyptian victories: 'In the eighth year of his reign, the Sea Peoples invaded Egypt by land and sea', and two Libyan campaigns in the Western Delta; the defeated were incorporated as subjects and 'settled in Southern Canaan'.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the Nile valley's desert edges, the Nubian posts (Buhen, the Fourth Cataract), the Canaanite and Syrian tributaries.
